title: Löwenstein–Jensen as a named solid medium
dek: Egg-based selective agar with a Wikipedia recipe history. Time-to-positivity and MGIT liquid culture stay on tb-smear-culture.
story: Löwenstein–Jensen on Wikipedia is the classic egg-based solid medium: malachite green to hold back contaminants, weeks of waiting, rough buff colonies if Mtb grows.

Modern labs often lead with liquid MGIT for speed and then use solid media as backup or for morphology. The clinic smear/culture plate owns that algorithm. This card names the slant students still see in photos.
Colony morphology is a hint, not a species. Canettii is smooth; some NTM are rapid growers on the same shelf.
deep: Middlebrook broths are a different Wikipedia/recipe family.
PZA testing is not an LJ colony color.
Contamination on LJ is a biosafety and quality story, not a resistance gene.
Do not delay WRD waiting for pretty slants.
